en: Do you remember this slide from earlier in
the course?
We can build 2 kinds of web apps basically
with Deno and with any server-side
technology in general.
We can build web apps that use server-side
rendered views or we build apps that
basically are APIs to which clients, mobile
apps, browsers can talk where then the
client is responsible for rendering what's
on the screen.
That's the difference to server-side
rendered views. There with server-side
rendered views, we return the finished views
from the server. With APIs, we return just
the data and it's the job of the frontend of
the client app to render a nice user
interface.
Now, since we had a look at how Deno can be
used to build a web app that returns views
based on templates,
in this module, we're now going to have a
look at how we can build REST APIs with
Deno.
As part of this module, we will, by the way,
also work with a database. So make sure you
definitely went through that database
section first so that you understand how
Deno can communicate with a database like
MongoDB.
With that, in this module, I will again
clarify what a REST API is exactly. We'll
talk about the data format that we're going
to use, the JSON data format, and most
importantly, we're going to build a complete
example application which now is built as a
REST API and not as a web app that returns
server-side rendered views.
